subject: Topology and Service-Boundary Annotation for SIG Questionnaire
messages:
From: security@acme-inc.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-20T16:08:00Z
Subject: SIG: topology and isolation details for Private deployment

Hi Kimberly,

We're wrapping up the SIG questionnaire for our audit and need an annotated network/service topology for Redwood's Private deployment that calls out tenant isolation, control-plane boundaries, egress controls, and where (if any) shared services exist. Specifically we need: 
- a diagram with labeled subnets/VPCs and control-plane endpoints
- a short narrative describing traffic flows (inbound management, inference data in/out, telemetry/metrics)
- a statement of encryption-in-transit and at-rest boundaries for customer data

Can you provide that as a PDF and a CSV mapping of control-plane egress destinations? Our deadline is EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Alice McCarthy
Security Operations, Acme Inc.
security@acme-inc.com

[Attachment requested: template_SIG_topology.xlsx]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: security@acme-inc.com, alice.mccarthy@acme-inc.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-20T18:34:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG: topology and isolation details for Private deployment

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide an annotated topology and the required mapping. High-level notes before I attach the first pass:

1) Topology scope: the artifact covers Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC + Redwood control plane peering model) for our US region. It excludes on-prem air-gapped installs — we can provide a separate runbook for that if needed.

2) Key isolation controls called out in the PDF:
   - Tenant compute nodes run in customer VPC/private subnets (no cross-tenant routing).
   - Control plane endpoints are in a Redwood-managed VPC; access to them is restricted via mutually authenticated TLS and IP allow-lists per customer.
   - KV cache and model artifacts are mounted to inference workers using ephemeral encrypted volumes (AES-256), and keys are stored in customer KMS when configured.
   - Egress from inference workers to public internet is routed through a dedicated egress NAT in customer VPC with optional centralized proxy. We list allowed destinations in the CSV.

3) Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+ (mutual TLS for control plane RPCs), at-rest AES-256 for model caches and persisted artifacts. Customer data retention boundaries are documented in the PDF.

I've attached: private_topology_annotated_v1.pdf (diagram + narrative), control-plane-egress-matrix.csv (hostname/IP + purpose).

Next steps: Priyom will add operational runbook notes (bastion access, maintenance windows). Karthik will add SOC2/SIG references for each control. If you want a redacted copy (no customer IPs) for external sharing, say the word and we'll produce it.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
[attachment: private_topology_annotated_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.6MB)]
[attachment: control-plane-egress-matrix.csv (csv, 18KB)]

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, alice.mccarthy@acme-inc.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T02:11:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG: topology and isolation details for Private deployment

Adding operational annotations and a short runbook stub. Extracts below (full runbook attached):

- Bastion access: Admin access to customer VPC (for maintenance/debug) is via temporary ephemeral bastion sessions using OIDC-backed jumpbox accounts; sessions are logged to our central audit log (immutable) and forwarded to customer's SIEM on request.
- KV cache purge/rotation: key rotation events are handled via Citadel (internal service) and depend on customer KMS schedule if customer-managed keys are used.
- Model rollout isolation: during canary rollouts we pin model shards to a subset of worker pools; cross-tenant eviction is enforced by hypervisor-level namespace enforcement.

I've attached runbook_private_deploy.md with the following sections: maintenance workflow, emergency rollback steps, evidence pointers (links to audit logs), and a minimal checklist for SOC2 evidence collection.

-- Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
[attachment: runbook_private_deploy.md (md, 24KB)]

From: alice.mccarthy@acme-inc.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T09:42:00Z

Kimberly — this is great, thank you. The diagram and CSV cover the items the auditors flagged. A few quick follow-ups: 
- Can you add a one-paragraph justification for why the control plane IP allow-list is sufficient versus per-connection firewalling for our compliance packet?
- Would you be able to provide a redacted (no customer CIDRs) PDF for our security attestation?

If you can get those two items by EOD today that will let us finish the SIG and close the ticket. We're copying Karthik to confirm the language for the compliance packet.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Alice
Alice McCarthy
Security Operations, Acme Inc.
